如果you could go back to the early days of the internet, would you handle your privacy differently? Most people would. We would have been more selective about the services we joined and the information we shared. Since a time machine isn't an option, we have to face reality. Your personal data is being openly bought and sold today.

Your phone number, email address, home address, and even your family relationships are now being packaged and resold to marketing firms, insurance companies, and hackers. While Safari and Mail's built-in privacy features can block some tracking as you browse, they can't erase data that has been harvested over the years and spread across hundreds of intermediary databases. Data brokers have built a multi-billion dollar industry by collecting, packaging, and selling your digital information. It's time to take your personal data off the market and off the internet. Let's take a look at how.

Security risks posed by data brokers

However, the dangers go far beyond annoying spam calls. When your information is readily available, you become an easy target for sophisticated cyberattacks. Since this industry is largely unregulated, your most private information and details—including past jobs, places you've lived, old loans, and more—can be easily purchased, posing significant security concerns.

Modern scammers leverage broker data to craft highly personalized and hard-to-detect phishing attacks. When scammers already know your job title, places you've lived, and even the names of your colleagues and friends, they can easily bypass your defensive instincts. As long as a scammer knows you inside and out, they only need to strike when your guard is down, dramatically increasing their chances of success.

For those concerned about personal safety, these sites and brokers act like a searchable public database, offering convenience for harassers and stalkers. By mapping the relationship networks of your friends, family, and neighbors, brokers provide a tracking blueprint for individuals who deliberately keep a low profile and hide their whereabouts.

The solution: Incogni automated data removal service

This ecosystem is massive and, frankly, daunting. Filing removal requests with hundreds of sites one by one is practically a full-time job—and has a very low success rate—because if it were easy, these brokers would have gone out of business long ago. What you need is a solution that understands how this industry works and knows all the tricks, helping you reclaim control over your right to privacy.

Precisely because of this, services like Incogni have become critical to both your digital world and real life. This service transforms the major problem you face—your data being everywhere and sold—into a solved problem, taking a one-stop-shop approach. You don't need to spend months tracking down data brokers one by one; Incogni automatically handles those repetitive and tedious opt-out processes on your behalf. They ensure your data isn't just removed once, but is continuously monitored and maintained, because brokers will inevitably try to re-harvest it.

Incogni's comprehensive dashboard lets you track the progress of your personal data removals in real time, including:

  • Number of databases that may hold your data
  • Removal requests being sent out on your behalf
  • Completed removal items and ongoing follow-ups

The real benefits of data removal for privacy-minded individuals

Removing your information from internet broker databases can deliver immediate results for you and your family

  • When companies can't buy your number, scam calls and spam texts decrease.
  • Scammers lose their target leads. Identity thieves typically obtain victim information from broker sites.
  • Your home address stays private, making it harder for stalkers and harassers to find your residence.
  • Your credit score stays healthy, as reduced data exposure lowers the risk of identity theft and strengthens your overall financial health.
